findings: components[1].sound_limitation.text incorrectly says the modern pair is separate evidence and does not establish the ancient relation. The entry already supplies Modern Mandarin 其 qí : 期 qī, and the cited local Unihan rows support those values. Replace that clause with a limitation confined to the historical comparison: the Baxter–Sagart readings are compatible with a sound relationship but do not by themselves establish 其’s role in the graph; the modern pair is a separate, current comparison. Cite the applicable reading evidence (X-a59bc3185f3948018041, X-dc1d185e2ef3b8cbaee2).

learner.components[1].text says the historical readings support a sound relationship, but cites only X-46947e4ca1764318e490, which is sufficient for the shared Middle Chinese form and similar, distinct Old Chinese forms. Qualify the claim as compatibility rather than proof, for example: “The historical readings are compatible with a sound relationship, though they do not prove it.”

history[1].text states that the sign 其 was reused for 期 because their spoken forms were similar, but the evidence says the basket’s original spoken name is not established and does not independently verify that sound match. Qualify the reason as a proposed borrowing mechanism: 其 was used to write 期, plausibly because of sound similarity, while the old basket name and the match remain unconfirmed (X-19d01d81c754a7a17098, X-ef8e176d1f8708c44701).
